title: Streaming metadata envelope and granular ACK protocol
creator: Asha Patel
description: Upgrade our SSE streaming implementation to send a small JSON metadata envelope per chunk and introduce a granular ACK/sequence model. Goals: make reconnect behavior deterministic for clients, enable partial replay and deduplication based on sequence/checksum, and carry structured tool-call boundaries and structured-output hints in the stream without breaking older clients. This ticket scopes the framing format, server-side retention window, handshake negotiation, and SDK compatibility plan.
acceptance_criteria: Server emits a per-chunk JSON envelope with fields: seq, prev_hash, checksum, type, meta (model_tokens, kv_offset), and length_hint
Clients can request a sync by sending last_seq in reconnect metadata and receive only missing seq > last_seq
Stream handshake supports negotiation via X-Redwood-Stream-Version header: v1 (legacy) and v2 (envelope). v1 remains default for existing clients unless negotiated
Tool/function-call boundaries are labeled with type="tool_call" and include canonical tool_id and a stable call_seq that survives reconnects
Server retains last N windows (configurable, default 1000 seqs) and exposes a sync_token for longer-lived clients
End-to-end integration tests for reconnect, duplicate-suppression, and partial-replay pass in CI with >= 95% success on simulated packet loss
SDKs (python/node) updated with transparent fallback and example migration guide in docs
Performance regression < 2% p99 latency overhead at typical payload sizes (<= 1024 tokens) compared to baseline streaming implementation
implementation_notes: Framing: each SSE data event will contain a single JSON object representing the envelope plus a base64-encoded payload field for the chunk bytes (or raw text for text-only chunks). Avoid multi-line SSE events to reduce client reassembly complexity.

Envelope fields: seq (int), prev_hash (hex), checksum (crc32c hex), type(enum: delta, partial, final, tool_call, heartbeat), meta (string map flattened: model_tokens=NN;kv_offset=NN), length_hint (int)
Dedup logic: client ignores chunk if received seq <= last_applied_seq or if checksum matches applied seq. Server will mark seq as tombstoned after retention window expires.

Handshake: HTTP header X-Redwood-Stream-Version can be set by client; server will return chosen-version in X-Redwood-Stream-Version response header. If mismatch, server falls back to legacy SSE encoding and emits a warning event with code 1001.
Compatibility: legacy clients continue to receive the existing streaming format. New SDKs will default to v2 and perform a graceful downgrade if server cannot support v2.
Storage: ephemeral in-memory seq window per connection group; for Dedicated/private we add optional small Redis-backed window for cross-worker reconnects (feature flag off by default).

Tool-calls: a tool_call envelope will carry tool_id and call_seq. If a reconnect occurs mid-tool-call, client can replay from the last tool_call.seq and server will provide the remainder or a structured "error/resume" envelope.
Telemetry: add new metrics: streaming.seq_gap_count, streaming.reconnect_rate, streaming.checksum_mismatch_count. Expose these in Console runtime dashboard.
testing_plan: Integration: run reconnect scenarios (client-side restart, transient 30s outage) with fuzzed chunk drops and assert dedup and resume correctness
Load: simulate 10k concurrent streaming connections with mix of v1/v2 clients to measure p99 overhead
Chaos: inject reordered delivery and duplicated chunks to verify client dedup logic and server tombstone behavior
SDK e2e: python and node SDK test harnesses exercise graceful downgrade and tool_call boundary preservation
Observability: add dashboards and alerts for checksum_mismatch_count > 0.1% of streams over 5m window
